## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b660a8064672e2b14e1d3628e2b6e68eebd05464`
Local-runs: none
Scope: AGENTS.md, docs/NORTH-STAR.md + ROADMAP.md

Inputs read: card #35206 (body and all 3 comments: claim, os-dev-report, the seat's scope amendment of 15:01Z), epic #35205, the plan document (rev 28), PR #35214 body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base = `origin/main` 084156de, 3 files, +161 -108), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept set, schema, export or runtime surface changes: the diff is three prose files. Right.
- `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` road rows: 80 rows at base, 80 at head; with the leading field removed the two sorted lists are byte-identical. Only the leading `axis` became the road step (8/48/6/9/6/3 over steps 1 to 6, the same counts as the six base headings). No checklist item id moved out of the page or was duplicated, so "every item belongs to exactly one row" still holds. Right.
- No script in the tree parses the North Star's rows, headings or the `axis` field (grep at head: every script hit is the governed-path register, not the content), so dropping the six step headings and the `axis` field breaks no gate. Right.
- Grade cells against the plan, cell by cell: Bug table 4 x 4 (Severe · data wrong p1/p1/p1/p2 with the unrecoverable or cross-tenant carve-out; Broken p1/p1/p2/p2; Impeded p2/p2/p2/p3; Cosmetic p2/p3/p3/p3) and the security table 3 x 2 (p1/p2, p1/p2, p2 with the platform-administrator or cross-tenant carve-out / p3) all match, column order included. The new cell Broken x builders = p1 is present. Right.
- Product areas table against the plan: nine rows, coverage, core features (5/4/6/4/6/4) and status match; the card-count column and card numbers are left out, which the page's own "carries no numbers" rule requires. Right.
- Check-runs on the head at review time: no failure. Success on Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, tooling self-tests, Type Check · workspace and debt ledger. Still in progress with no conclusion, and therefore not claimed green by this record: Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · CI release and engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Test Core (1/10).

### ② Semver level

No package is published by this diff (root prose and `docs/` only), so `skip-changeset` is the matching level; both Check Changeset runs concluded skipped. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body agrees with the claim's `Clause-②: no (rule text, no schema, export or accept set)` and with the diff. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, p0 wording (PR Acceptance notes and the report's judgement call): NOT accepted as it stands. See S1; the choice of wording is escalated to the maintainer on the card.
- Dev flag, seven boundary row placements: answered, accepted. Each follows a boundary line of the plan (i18n always to `area:ux`; the numbers to `area:data`, the API to `area:workflow`; upgrades and migrations to `area:package`; expressions written in metadata to `area:build`). Row placement carries no grade under the new rules, so no placement changes a verdict.
- Dev flag, model-named co-author trailer on the first commit: answered. Squash merge takes the PR title and body; the trailer does not reach `main`. No action on this head.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope stale references left to #35207: accepted as routed, but the list is short. Beside `filing-gate.md`:55 and `SKILL.md`:128, these also cite text this PR deletes and belong on #35207: `references/execution-duties.md`:50 (Priority rule 3 "with its exemption", the P0/P1 hold that no longer exists), `references/filing-gate.md`:41 to 69 (rule 2's "neither on the road nor on the checklist is p3"), `references/triage-duties.md`:68 (Priority rules 1 to 3 and the road-step `Path:` field).
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff; no id materialisation, no in-app join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, against epic #35205 and the plan:

S1 (should-fix) — the page now gives two answers for p0, and the conflict lands on the epic's own headline cell. The unchanged road paragraph (line 11) still says "The first step that breaks is the current P0". The new rule 2 grades the same event as Broken x "Builders, often (on the build, install and upgrade path)" = p1, and the plan states p0 as ONLY three cases (its dispatch list says 只有: main or the merge queue red, a release blocker inside the release window, a hole exploited in production). The head's p0 bullet lists the three cases but drops "only", so nothing on the page settles which sentence wins, and rule 3 gives p0 the right to pass every concurrency cap. Before this PR the two agreed (old rule 2: "the road broken is P0/P1"); this diff creates the split. `ROADMAP.md` repeats the old reading twice ("the first step that breaks is the current P0"; "Which step is P0 at any moment is decided by the weekly walk"). Fix on the prose face: either state the three cases as the only p0 and reword line 11 and the two ROADMAP sentences to "graded by Priority rule 2", or carry a maintainer ruling on the card that a broken road step stays p0 and name it as a fourth case in the bullet. The dev flagged it as the maintainer's call; it needs that call before merge, not after.

N1 (nit) — rule 2 says "A Feature never enters p1" as an absolute, and the exception (a card blocking another repository's p1, "a Feature included") sits four bullets lower. Both sentences are the plan's; putting "except as below" on the first would stop a reader who stops there.

N2 (nit) — "Instruments serve the fleet" (unchanged) still says a fleet card "competes with product cards on the same field"; under the new rule 3 the field is the named area, and the fleet row of the area table already points at this paragraph. Wording only; the grading question it asks is unchanged.

Otherwise the file holds. Rules 2 and 3 carry every extra rule the epic lists (Feature never p1, Task default p3 rising to p2 only when it blocks dispatched work, the other-repository p1 inheritance, p1 ahead of every area including paused ones, a paused area no longer demotes, in-flight cards not regraded, the weekly re-check over ten). The deleted sentence "top to bottom is the order" is gone and nothing on the page re-states it. Severity definitions, the type definitions and the eight boundary lines are the plan's. Rules 1 and 4 and the last four sections are byte-unchanged.

`AGENTS.md` rule 8: the sentence now names "a core feature of its Product areas or a Features on the road row, graded by Priority". Both section names exist at head with those exact titles; "ladder" is gone and no other line of the file speaks of the table's order. Holds.

`ROADMAP.md` (implementing file, seat-widened to its header): the header agrees with the North Star at head. N3 (nit) — the body was outside the widened lines and now disagrees with its own header: "The order above follows the table" (the table is grouped by area, not by step) and "`area:*` labels for one feature axis and `priority:*` for order" (the grade no longer orders). The two P0 sentences are part of S1; the rest is a follow-up for #35207 or a card of its own.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1) open on this head; N1 to N3 are nits.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Scope: AGENTS.md, docs/NORTH-STAR.md + ROADMAP.md
Security-touching: yes

Delta review of the record on `b660a8064672e2b14e1d3628e2b6e68eebd05464` (PR comment 6982541233). Read this round: the two commits between that head and this one (`docs/NORTH-STAR.md` +7 -6, `ROADMAP.md` +4 -4; `AGENTS.md` untouched), epic #35205 comments 6982539552 (15:08Z: cloud aligns, rule (a), rule (b)) and 6982581146 (15:10Z: the maintainer's choice that makes rule (a) exact), the plan document at rev 29, the page at this head, and the check-runs on this head. Card #35206 carries no new comment. Everything the earlier record judged and these commits did not touch stands as judged there. The intermediate head e0cd15e9 was read but no record was posted on it; a finding raised there (the paraphrased UX sentence promised a p1 the table could not reach) does not exist on this head, because that sentence is gone.

### ① Derived judgments

- Still prose only: no accept set, schema, export or runtime surface. Right.
- No road row and no grade cell moved: both grading tables and the Product areas table are byte-unchanged from the reviewed head, so the cell-by-cell match with the plan holds at rev 29 too (the plan's tables did not change between rev 28 and rev 29). Right.
- Check-runs on this head at review time: Governed Surface Queue Guard success; PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links and Check PR Size in progress; no Lint or Type Check family had reported. No failure; this record claims no gate verdict beyond the one success.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: nothing published, `skip-changeset` still on the PR, `Clause-②: no` still matches the diff. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- S1 from the earlier record: answered by the fix, see below.
- The seat's ask in 6982539552 (rules (a) and (b) into this PR, at most one pointer sentence about cloud): one sentence, "The cloud repository follows these rules with its own areas and core features." It agrees with "Cloud aligns" and contradicts neither the `area:cloud` row nor "Not now". Accepted.
- Escalated, not a finding on the diff: the page says a card in flight "may be raised, never lowered". That is the third bullet of rule (a) in 6982539552. Comment 6982581146 restates rule (a) as three items and does not repeat it, and the plan at rev 29 still reads 在飞的卡（已派出或有人认领）不改级. The head follows the newer epic record; the plan sentence needs syncing, or the seat confirms on the card that the raise permission stands, before the maintainer merges.
- Stale pm-dispatch citations listed in the earlier record stay with #35207; these commits add none.
- SQL push-down: no code. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed. The road paragraph no longer names a P0: a step that breaks is "graded by Priority rule 2 ... Broken × builders, p1", the table's own cell. The p0 bullet reads "and only these" before the plan's three cases. `ROADMAP.md` says the first broken step "goes ahead of other work" and that the walk decides "which step is broken". The page gives one answer for p0.

N1: closed. The never-p1 sentence carries its exception inline ("unless it blocks another repository's p1, below").

N3: closed. `ROADMAP.md` body: the grouping follows the steps of the road and is not an order of work; `priority:*` decides what jumps the queue.

N2: left as an accepted deviation (unchanged maintainer text in "Instruments serve the fleet"); wording only.

The UX rule, against 6982581146 and plan rev 29: holds, sentence by sentence.
- "a UX problem on a core feature that every user hits every time is p1; every other UX problem is p2. UX has no p3." These are items 1 and 2 of the comment, and the plan's 核心功能上每个用户每次都碰到的 → p1；其余 → p2，体验类不再有 p3.
- "for `area:ux` and for an experience problem in any other area" is the plan's scope clause (`area:ux` 和其他专题里的体验问题).
- "A Feature that improves UX defaults to p2; any other Feature never enters p1 (unless it blocks another repository's p1, below)" is item 3 and the plan's sentence, in the same order.
- Precedence is stated twice, so the rule and the Bug table cannot both claim a card: step two opens "only Bug cards and security cards are graded by the two tables below, and UX problems by the UX rule below", and the line above the table says "a UX problem takes the UX rule below instead". The p1 is now reached by the rule itself and no longer depends on which severity a UX problem is read as.
- Tried against the rest of the page: the p3-closed-at-first-touch bullet covers only cards "with no effect on users", so it does not hand a UX problem a p3; rule 3's order and the weekly re-check over ten p1 cards are unaffected; rule 4's "looking wrong is as much a defect as failing to render" agrees.

Rule (b), repository before area: holds. "judge the repository first (a platform root cause is fixed in this repository, wherever it shows up)" is the comment's sentence, and it does not collide with the `area:cloud` boundary, which picks the area inside this repository.

N4 (nit) — the page states no default grade for a Feature outside UX ("done in its area's order"); the plan is silent too. A follow-up at most.

N5 (nit) — with the UX rule in force the table's Cosmetic row ("looks wrong, wording, consistency, small experience") and Impeded's "an error that cannot be understood" describe what the area boundary already calls a UX problem, so the Cosmetic p3 cells have almost no card left to grade. The precedence clause settles every case, and the plan keeps both the table and the rule, so the cells stay as the plan's; one sentence saying what a non-UX Cosmetic card is would help triage and can ride #35207.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
